Description:
Objective

Provide a guided ticket intake and classification process for support tickets.

 Context

The goal is to make sure support tickets enter the workflow with enough business information, consistent categories, and clear review flags. This work is part of Release 1 — Core. It relates to HLR-01, HLR-02, HLR-04, and HLR-08, as well as FR-01 to FR-07 and FR-09 to FR-15.

 Scope

Included:

* Collect structured issue, impact, workaround, and customer-account information
* Validate required information
* Retrieve customer organisation and subscription details
* Assign one of the seven approved ticket categories
* Record category changes for audit purposes
* Provide ticket-creation confirmation to the customer

Not included:

* N/A

 Success criteria

* Tickets are created with structured issue, impact, workaround, and customer-account information
* Required information is validated
* Customer organisation and subscription details are retrieved
* Incomplete submissions are flagged as *Information Required*
* Unidentified accounts are flagged as *Account Verification Required*
* Tickets are assigned one of the seven approved categories
* Uncertain classifications are flagged as *Category Review Required*
* Category changes are recorded for audit purposes
* Customers receive ticket-creation confirmation

 Risks and dependencies

* Depends on retrieving customer organisation and subscription details
* Depends on having the seven approved ticket categories available
* Depends on clear rules for identifying incomplete submissions, unidentified accounts, and uncertain classifications

 Other information

* MoSCoW priority: Must Have
* Release: Release 1 — Core

Summary

As a customer, I want to provide structured information about my support issue so the support team can understand and process my request correctly.

 Context

The issue is about a support intake chatbot that collects and validates customer issue details before creating a ticket.

 Acceptance criteria

* The intake chatbot captures:
** issue description
** affected users
** impact on core functionality
** workaround availability
** business email
* The system validates the required information and clearly identifies missing or unclear details.
* When the business email matches an account, the system retrieves:
** customer organization
** subscription tier
** plan status
* If the account cannot be identified, the ticket displays *Account Verification Required* and receives a provisional priority based on the reported business impact until the account is verified.
* An incomplete submission is still created as a ticket and displays *Information Required* instead of being rejected. The assigned agent can request and update the missing information.
* After ticket creation, the customer receives:
** the ticket ID
** assigned or provisional priority
** expected first-response time

 Other information

* Related requirements:
** HLR-01, HLR-04
** FR-01 to FR-07, FR-09
* Related UAT:
** UAT-04

Summary

As a Support Agent, I want the system to recommend a ticket category and flag uncertain classifications so that tickets can be reviewed and routed consistently.

 Context

The feature is meant to support consistent ticket routing. It applies after complete ticket information is submitted.

 Acceptance criteria

# The system uses the issue description and structured intake responses to recommend one of the seven approved ticket categories after complete ticket information is submitted.
# Uncertain or unclear classifications are flagged for manual review.
# The ticket displays “Category Review Required” until the review is completed.
# When an agent changes the automatically assigned category, the system records:
#* the original category
#* the final category
#* the agent
#* the date and time of the change
# The assigned category is displayed on the ticket record and in the agent queue without requiring the agent to open the ticket.

Objective

Assign each ticket a consistent severity and priority, then route it to an eligible Support Agent using approved business rules.

 Context

This epic covers core priority assignment and basic routing for support tickets.  
It aligns with related high-level requirements HLR-03, HLR-04, HLR-05, and HLR-11, plus primary functional requirements FR-08 and FR-16 to FR-33.  
It also follows related rules PM-01 to PM-04, BR-01 to BR-06, KD-01 to KD-05, and ER-14.

 Scope

Included:

* Classify severity as Critical, High, Medium, or Low
* Apply priority-override rules before the standard priority matrix
* Assign P1, P2, or P3 using severity, customer impact, and subscription tier
* Flag contradictory information as Priority Review Required
* Assign a provisional higher priority until agent review
* Record priority changes for audit purposes
* Recalculate routing and SLA deadlines after a priority change
* Route tickets using category skill, availability, workload, and P1 eligibility
* Display Manual Assignment Required when no eligible P1 agent is available
* Alert the Team Lead when manual P1 assignment is required

Not included:

* FR-29, which is planned for Release 2 — Enhancement
* Experience-based routing tie-breaker, which is listed as a Should Have

 Success criteria

* Each ticket is assigned a consistent severity and priority
* Priority-override rules are applied before the standard priority matrix
* Tickets are assigned P1, P2, or P3 based on the defined inputs
* Contradictory information is flagged as Priority Review Required
* A provisional higher priority is assigned until agent review
* Priority changes are recorded for audit purposes
* Routing and SLA deadlines are recalculated after any priority change
* Tickets are routed using category skill, availability, workload, and P1 eligibility
* Manual Assignment Required is shown when no eligible P1 agent is available
* The Team Lead is alerted when manual P1 assignment is required

 Risks and dependencies

* Correct implementation depends on the approved business rules
* Routing depends on accurate agent category skill, availability, workload, and P1 eligibility data
* SLA recalculation depends on priority change handling working correctly
* Manual P1 assignment requires Team Lead alerting to function as expected
* Release 2 work is dependent on FR-29 being handled separately

 Other information

* MoSCoW priority: Must Have — core priority assignment and basic routing
* MoSCoW priority: Should Have — experience-based routing tie-breaker
* Release: Release 1 — Core
* FR-29 planned for Release 2 — Enhancement

Summary: Assign severity and priority using approved rules
Description:
Summary

As a Support Agent, I want the system to assign ticket severity and priority using approved business rules so that urgent tickets are identified consistently..

 Context

This user story is for Support Agents. It is part of Release 1 - Core and is marked as a Must Have.

 Acceptance criteria

* The system classifies severity as Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
* Severity must be based on:
** affected users
** core-function impact
** workaround availability
** issue details
* The system checks approved priority-override rules before applying the standard priority matrix.
* Complete organisation-wide blockage without a workaround must be assigned P1, regardless of subscription tier.
* Organisation-wide or multi-user authentication failure must be assigned P1, regardless of subscription tier.
* When no override applies, the system combines severity and subscription tier to assign P1, P2, or P3 using the approved priority matrix.
* The assigned priority must be visible on the ticket and in the agent queue without opening the ticket.
* Ticket category alone must not determine priority.

As a Support Agent, I want conflicting ticket information and provisional priorities to be flagged so that I can review and confirm the correct priority.

# When the detected impact appears higher than the selected impact, the system assigns a provisional higher priority and notifies the assigned agent.

#* system-assigned severity

#* final priority
#* applied rule
#* reason for change

#* date and time

As a Team Lead, I want tickets to be routed to suitable and available Support Agents so that assignments are consistent and P1 tickets are handled only by eligible agents.

 Context

The routing should use agent suitability and availability rules.

 Acceptance criteria

# Automatic routing starts after the ticket category and priority have been assigned.
# The system considers:
#* category skill
#* current availability
#* active workload
#* priority-handling eligibility
when selecting an agent.
# Only agents available during the active support shift can receive new tickets.
# When multiple eligible agents are available, the system prioritizes the agent with the lower active workload.

#* the ticket priority changes
#* the assigned agent becomes unavailable
#* the Team Lead requests reassignment

Summary: Track SLA deadlines and provide early warnings
Description:
Summary

As a Team Lead, I want SLA deadlines and early-warning indicators to be visible so that I can intervene before avoidable breaches occur.

 Context

This issue is related to tracking SLA deadlines for tickets. It is part of Release 1 — Core and has a MoSCoW priority of Must Have.

 Acceptance criteria

# The system calculates the SLA start time using approved business hours and excludes company holidays.
# The system calculates and displays the first response and resolution deadlines according to ticket priority. It also applies the approved workaround targets: P1 - 4 business hours where possible, P2 - 8 business hours where possible, and P3 - no workaround target.
# Active tickets display the time remaining, any warning or breach indicator, and the current SLA status: Normal, At Risk, Met, Breached, or Paused where applicable.
# A P1 ticket without a personalised first response is marked At Risk after 10 minutes, and the Team Lead is alerted.
# P2 and P3 tickets are marked At Risk, and the Team Lead is alerted after 3 and 6 business hours respectively when no personalised first response has been provided.
# An unresolved ticket is marked At Risk and the Team Lead is alerted after 10 business hours for P1, 24 business hours for P2, or 40 business hours for P3. Approved resolution-SLA pause time is excluded.
# An automated ticket acknowledgement does not count as a personalised first response.
# Customer follow-ups do not restart or extend the SLA timer.

Summary

Escalate qualifying SLA breaches and operational exceptions to the Team Lead so serious support risks receive timely attention.

User story:

As a Team Lead, I want qualifying SLA breaches and operational exceptions to be escalated consistently so that serious support risks receive timely attention.

 Acceptance criteria

# A ticket is formally escalated to the Team Lead when its first-response SLA is breached:
#* P1: 15 minutes
#* P2: 4 business hours
#* P3: 8 business hours
# A ticket is formally escalated when its resolution SLA is breached:
#* P1: 12 business hours
#* P2: 30 business hours
#* P3: 48 business hours
# A third customer follow-up within four hours of ticket creation triggers Team Lead escalation, but does not automatically change the ticket priority.
# If no eligible P1 agent is available, the Team Lead is alerted immediately and the ticket displays Manual Assignment Required.
# An Enterprise P1 ticket is escalated to the Customer Support Head when the Team Lead requests senior involvement or when it remains unresolved for two hours after Team Lead escalation.

#* reason
#* level
#* date and time
#* notified person
#* current owner
#* action taken
#* closure details
# An SLA breach remains recorded even if the ticket is later responded to or resolved.
# The resolution SLA can be paused only when required customer information is pending or resolution depends on an approved external third party. A P1 SLA pause requires Team Lead approval.
# For every SLA pause, the system records the pause reason, pause start time, resume time and person approving the pause.
# When a ticket priority is upgraded, the system recalculates the applicable SLA deadline from the original SLA start time. The SLA timer does not restart.

Objective

Keep customers informed throughout the ticket lifecycle and maintain a traceable history of all customer notifications.

 Context

This Epic covers ticket-creation confirmation, escalation updates, updated timelines, resolution notifications and notification-delivery records.

 Scope

Included:

* Send ticket-creation confirmation containing the ticket ID, assigned or provisional priority and expected first-response time
* Send an escalation notification when the ticket receives additional management review
* Provide an updated response or resolution timeline when applicable
* Send resolution confirmation containing the documented resolution summary, resolution date and time, and instructions for reopening the issue or raising a new ticket if the problem continues
* Record notification type, recipient, date and time, and delivery status
* Provide an optional customer-satisfaction survey after resolution
* If a notification cannot be delivered, mark it as Failed, alert the assigned agent, and allow the agent to resend it or use an approved alternative communication method

 Success criteria

* Customers receive confirmation after a ticket is created
* Customers receive an update when their ticket is escalated
* Resolution confirmation is sent only after the resolution has been documented
* Notification history records the message type, recipient, date and time, and delivery status
* The optional customer-satisfaction survey can be enabled as a future enhancement
* Resolution confirmations include the documented resolution summary, resolution date and time, and appropriate next-step instructions
* Failed notifications remain visible, the assigned agent is alerted, and resend or approved alternative communication is available

 Requirements

High-level requirements:

HLR-08, HLR-11

Functional requirements:

FR-09, FR-47, FR-59 to FR-63

Non-functional requirements:

NFR-06 to NFR-08

 Risks and dependencies

* Notifications depend on a valid customer business email
* Escalation notifications depend on an approved escalation event
* Resolution confirmation depends on a completed resolution summary
* Notification-service failure may delay an important customer update; failed delivery must be recorded and followed up by the assigned agent through resend or an approved alternative communication method
* The customer-satisfaction survey is not required for Release 1

 Prioritization and release

MoSCoW priority:

* Must Have — core customer notifications and notification history
* Could Have — customer-satisfaction survey

Release:

* Release 1 — Core notifications
* Future Backlog — customer-satisfaction survey

Objective

Provide authorized support-management users with a current operational view of ticket workload, SLA risk and escalations so they can identify issues requiring attention and take appropriate action.

 Context

This Epic covers the operational dashboard for the Team Lead and Customer Support Head. It provides management visibility but does not replace the underlying ticket, routing, SLA-monitoring or escalation functions.

The dashboard is a Should Have capability planned for Release 2 — Enhancement. Advanced analytics, predictive SLA forecasting and business-intelligence reporting are outside the approved scope.

 Scope

Included:

* Restrict dashboard access to the Team Lead and Customer Support Head by default
* Allow Support Agent access to management-level information only when specifically authorized
* Display open tickets by:
** priority
** category
** status
** customer tier
* Highlight tickets approaching an SLA breach
* Display tickets that have already breached an SLA
* Display the time remaining before each applicable deadline
* Order At Risk tickets by the nearest SLA deadline
* Display currently escalated tickets, including:
** escalation reason
** escalation level
** current ticket owner
** time since escalation
* Display the number of active tickets assigned to each Support Agent
* Display first-response and resolution SLA-compliance percentages separately
* Allow filtering by:
** priority
** category
** status
** customer tier
** assigned agent
** SLA status
* Allow authorized users to open the relevant ticket directly from the dashboard, subject to their existing permissions
* Reflect changes to ticket status, priority, assignment, SLA risk or escalation status within one minute
* Require secure authentication and role-based access for management information

 Success criteria

* The Team Lead and Customer Support Head can review the current support queue from one operational view
* At Risk tickets are clearly identified and ordered by the nearest SLA deadline
* Current escalations, ownership and agent workload are visible
* First-response and resolution SLA compliance are displayed separately
* Authorized users can filter dashboard information and open relevant tickets for review or action
* Applicable ticket and SLA changes appear on the dashboard within one minute
* Management-level information is not visible to unauthorized users

 Requirements

High-level requirement:

* HLR-09

Functional requirements:

* FR-49 to FR-58

Non-functional requirements:

* NFR-03
* NFR-06 to NFR-08

 Risks and dependencies

* Dashboard information depends on accurate ticket, assignment, SLA and escalation data
* SLA-risk visibility depends on the approved SLA calculations and warning rules
* Workload visibility depends on current ticket-ownership information
* The one-minute update requirement requires technical validation during design and testing
* Dashboard access depends on correctly configured authentication and role-based permissions
* The dashboard is an operational view and does not include predictive analytics or advanced business-intelligence reporting

 Prioritization and release

MoSCoW priority:

* Should Have

Release:

* Release 2 — Enhancement

Objective

Enable authorized System Administrators to manage approved operational rules without routine code changes.  
Ensure every configuration change is validated, approved, traceable, and recoverable.

 Context

This Epic covers configuration of priority rules, SLA targets, escalation thresholds, and routing criteria.

It includes Release 2 enhancement work for configuration access, rule updates, validation, approval, change history, version retention, and restoration of an earlier approved version.

A dedicated operational rollback workflow, including an explicit rollback record when a new configuration causes a problem, is kept in the Future Backlog.

 Scope

Included:

* Provide a configuration area accessible only to authorized System Administrators
* Require company-approved secure authentication and multi-factor authentication for privileged configuration access
* Allow authorized System Administrators to update approved:
** priority rules
** SLA targets
** escalation thresholds
** routing criteria
* Allow these updates through the system interface without requiring code changes
* Check configuration changes for:
** missing values
** invalid time limits
** conflicting rules
* Prevent an invalid configuration from being activated
* Show a clear explanation of what must be corrected
* Submit configuration changes to the Customer Support Head for review
* Notify the Customer Support Head when a change is waiting for approval
* Allow the Customer Support Head to approve or reject a submitted change
* Prevent a configuration change from becoming active before approval
* Retain previous approved configuration versions for review
* Allow an authorized user to restore an earlier approved version when required
* Record for every configuration change:
** rule or value changed
** previous value
** new value
** person making the change
** person approving the change
** date and time
** reason for the change
* Provide a Future Backlog rollback workflow when an approved change causes an operational problem
* Record any future rollback action in the configuration history

Out of scope:

* Broader product-code changes
* Detailed technical validation logic, which will be defined during solution design and testing

 Success criteria

* Only authorized System Administrators can access configuration functions
* Approved operational rules can be updated without routine code changes
* Invalid or conflicting configurations cannot be activated
* Users receive a clear explanation when configuration validation fails
* No configuration change becomes active before Customer Support Head approval
* Previous and current configuration values remain traceable
* Earlier approved versions can be reviewed and restored by an authorized user
* Every configuration change retains complete maker, approver, time, and reason information
* A future rollback workflow can restore a previously approved configuration and record the rollback action

 Risks and dependencies

* Incorrect configuration could affect ticket priority, SLA, escalation, or routing behaviour
* Configuration security depends on correctly implemented authentication and role-based access
* Activation depends on timely review by the Customer Support Head
* Version restoration and rollback depend on reliable approved-version history
* Detailed technical validation logic depends on solution design and testing

** FR-64 to FR-70
** NFR-06, NFR-08, NFR-12

Summary: Configure and validate approved operational rules
Description:
Summary

As a System Administrator, I want to configure and validate approved operational rules through the system interface. This helps prepare approved changes without routine code changes or invalid configurations affecting ticket handling.

 Context

This story covers authorized configuration access, rule editing, and validation. Approval, change history, and rollback are handled in separate stories.

This is a Should Have capability planned for Release 2 — Enhancement.

 Acceptance criteria

# Only authorized System Administrators can access the configuration area.
# Configuration access requires company-approved secure authentication and multi-factor authentication.
# The System Administrator can update approved:
#* priority rules
#* SLA targets
#* escalation thresholds
#* routing criteria
# Approved operational-rule changes can be prepared through the system interface without requiring code changes.
# Broader product-code or technical-architecture changes cannot be performed through the configuration area.
# Before a configuration change is saved or submitted, the system checks for:
#* missing required values
#* invalid time limits
#* conflicting rules
# If a validation error is found:
#* the configuration cannot be activated
#* the system identifies the error
#* the system clearly explains what must be corrected
# A valid configuration change can be submitted for approval but does not become active until the separate approval process is completed.
# Users can only view or change configuration information permitted for their assigned role.

 Other information

Related requirements:

* HLR-10
* FR-64, FR-65, FR-67
* NFR-06, NFR-08, NFR-12

Dependency:

* Activation depends on the configuration-approval Story.

Testing note:

* Detailed configuration-validation UAT will be prepared for Release 2. No execution result is claimed in the current portfolio baseline.

MoSCoW priority:

* Should Have

Release:

* Release 2 — Enhancement

Summary

As a Customer Support Head, I want configuration changes to be reviewed, approved and recorded before activation so that only authorized changes are applied and remain traceable.

 Context

This story covers configuration approval, retention of approved versions, basic restoration, and change history.

Configuration editing and validation are handled separately.

The dedicated rollback workflow for a configuration that causes an operational problem is a separate Future Backlog Story.

 Acceptance criteria

# When a valid configuration change is submitted, its status is recorded as *Pending Approval*.
# The Customer Support Head is notified that a configuration change is awaiting review.
# The Customer Support Head can review the proposed configuration change and either approve or reject it.
# A configuration change does not become active before it is approved by the Customer Support Head.
# An approved change can become active, while a rejected change remains inactive.
# For every configuration change, the system records:
#* rule or value changed
#* previous value
#* new value
#* person making the change
#* person approving the change
#* date and time
#* reason for the change
# The previous value remains preserved and is not overwritten by the new value.
# The system retains previous approved configuration versions for authorized review.
# An authorized user can select and restore a previous approved configuration version when required.
# Only approved configuration versions are eligible for restoration.
# A restoration remains visible in the configuration history.
# Users can only review, approve, or restore configuration information permitted for their assigned role.

 Other information

Related requirements:

* HLR-10, HLR-11
* FR-66, FR-68, FR-69
* NFR-06, NFR-08

Dependencies:

* A configuration must pass the separate validation process before it is submitted for approval.
* The Future Backlog rollback Story depends on approved-version history.

Testing note:

* Detailed approval, version-history, and restoration UAT will be prepared for Release 2. No execution result is claimed in the current portfolio baseline.

MoSCoW priority:

* Should Have

Release:

* Release 2 — Enhancement

Summary

As a System Administrator, I want to roll back a problematic configuration to a previously approved version so that I can restore a known working configuration without losing the change history.

 Context

This issue adds a dedicated rollback workflow for cases where an approved configuration change causes a problem.

Release 2 already provides approved-version history and basic restoration. This enhanced rollback workflow is a Could Have capability kept in the Future Backlog.

 Acceptance criteria

# An authorized System Administrator can start a rollback when the active configuration causes an operational problem.
# Only a previously approved configuration version can be selected for rollback.
# An unapproved, rejected, or incomplete configuration cannot be activated through the rollback process.
# The selected approved configuration is restored as the active configuration when the rollback is completed successfully.
# The rollback does not delete the problematic configuration or any earlier configuration history.
# For every rollback, the system records:
#* configuration version being replaced
#* approved version being restored
#* person initiating the rollback
#* date and time
#* reason for the rollback
#* rollback outcome
# The rollback record remains available in the configuration history.
# Rollback access requires company-approved secure authentication, multi-factor authentication, and the appropriate System Administrator permission.
# If the rollback cannot be completed, the system displays a clear message explaining the failure and the next action required.

 Other information

Related requirements:

* HLR-10, HLR-11
* FR-70
* NFR-06, NFR-08, NFR-12

Dependencies:

* Approved configuration-version history must be available.
* The version selected for rollback must already have been approved.

Testing note:

* Detailed rollback UAT will be prepared when this Future Backlog capability is selected for delivery. No execution result is claimed in the current portfolio baseline.

* Could Have

Release:
